newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish slightly lower.

text.p: French stocks finished slightly weaker on Tuesday in a consolidation prompted by Wall Street's drop on Monday, but bid speculation livened trading in financial shares, traders said.

They said the bourse was solidly underpinned by the strong performances of the bond markets and the dollar and a partial rebound on Wall Street in early trading, but many said a consolidation of the Paris market was welcome and overdue.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 13.28 points, or 0.51 percent, at 2,582.09, while the CAC-40 February futures contract fell 12 points to 2,591.

* Shares in computer design firm Dassault Systemes finished up 13.2 percent at 343 francs after the group reported a 55 percent jump in net income to 342.5 million francs for 1996. Several analysts said they had or would raise earnings estimates for 1997 and 1998 after the company increased its operating margin targets at an analysts' meeting.
* Cap Gemini also rose, adding 3.45 percent, to 306 francs, on better than expected results.
* Technip fell 3.88 percent at 545 francs after Morgan Stanley cut its recommendation on the energy services firm's stock to neutral after it reached the 550-560 objective.

* Michelin, which was weaker on profit-taking after racking up big gains this year, accelerated its losses to end 3.42 percent lower at 341.90 francs after a source at the European Commission said the tyremaker's sales practices in Europe were being probed. Michelin had no comment.

* Insurers AGF and GAN rose on speculative trading, fuelled by an article in La Tribune speculating on possible interest by Allianz in AGF. AGF closed up five percent at 189 francs. GAN shares closed up 6.76 percent at 112.10 francs.

* Societe Generale rose 0.45 percent to 665 francs, boosted by recent positive recommendations, while Suez, Paribas were hit by profit-taking. Suez fell 3.53 percent to 262.40 francs and Paribas fell 2.54 percent to 390.80 francs.
